title: `_requireNoBroadcastFlag` asserts an invariant it structurally cannot check (cheatcode string-literal scan misses inherited mutating helpers)
fingerprintNote: Carried VERBATIM from classified-findings.json; not recomputed by finding-manager.
description: Two compounding weaknesses in the verifier's safety story. (1) `_requireNoBroadcastFlag()` is named for a check it cannot perform — it only rejects PREVIEW_MODE (:97); its own NatSpec admits no cheatcode reports --broadcast. (2) `VerifyPromotionReady is DeployMainnetPromotionReady is Script, StdCheats`, so the compiled artifact retains StdCheats and the read-write `./server/deployments` fs_permissions grant, while test/VerifyPromotionReadyGuards.t.sol pins read-only-ness with raw substring scans for cheatcode LITERALS only ('startBroadcast','startPrank','vm.deal','vm.warp','forge-std/Test.sol','OLD_POOLER'). A future edit calling an inherited mutating helper — `_writeProgressFileWithStatus(...)` is the obvious one — would pass every current assertion, as would a live-read BPT fallback written through a local variable or a differently-named constant instead of the literal OLD_POOLER.
impact: None today, and the 'today' is verified rather than assumed. The verifier's complete call graph is run -> _requireNoBroadcastFlag / _loadAndValidateProgressFile / _adoptPersistedBptBaseline / _phase7_wiringAssertions / _verifyMintAuthorityInvariance / _printSummary — all view or storage-only. The closure-mapper independently confirmed that every phase function and every broadcast site in the inherited DeployMainnetPromotionReady is `internal` and uncalled from the verifier. The standalone run empirically mutated nothing (trace: vm.envOr plus a failed vm.readFile, then abort). A `:verify` run mistakenly given --broadcast is INERT, because no broadcast context is ever opened.
attackPath: 1. THE HAZARD THAT EXISTS NOW: a maintainer reads `_requireNoBroadcastFlag()` and believes the verifier rejects --broadcast. It does not; it only rejects PREVIEW_MODE (:97), as its own NatSpec admits. The maintainer's mental model of what protects the read-only leg is wrong. That is the entire present-day impact.

2. THE LATENT HAZARD (does not exist today): because `VerifyPromotionReady is DeployMainnetPromotionReady is Script, StdCheats`, the artifact retains StdCheats and the read-write ./server/deployments fs_permissions grant.

3. test/VerifyPromotionReadyGuards.t.sol:114-133 pins read-only-ness with raw substring scans for cheatcode LITERALS only ('startBroadcast', 'startPrank', 'vm.deal', 'vm.warp', 'forge-std/Test.sol', 'OLD_POOLER').

4. A future edit calling an INHERITED mutating helper — `_writeProgressFileWithStatus(...)` is the obvious one — contains none of those literals and would therefore pass every current assertion, as would a live-read BPT fallback routed through a local variable or a differently-named constant instead of the literal OLD_POOLER.
5. That edit does not exist. Step 4 is reachable only from code no one has written.
likelihood: n/a today. The present-day condition is certain (the name is wrong now) but its impact is maintainer comprehension. The exploitable condition is unreachable at c4396b1.
assumptions: For anything beyond a naming defect: a future edit introduces a call to an inherited mutating helper.
externalRequirements: None; and none suffice, because no such call site exists.
evidence: side-effects.json -> verifyLegStandalone, testHarnessAssessment, leadsResolution[0] and [1]. Source: VerifyPromotionReady.s.sol:89-98; test/VerifyPromotionReadyGuards.t.sol:114-133; foundry.toml fs_permissions read-write ./server/deployments.
justification: Downgraded from the auditor's Low to QA, and the downgrade is the conservative reading the evidence supports. C4 QA covers 'function incorrect as to spec, issues with comments' — a guard function whose NAME asserts an invariant it cannot check is that category exactly. The second half, the substring-only guard test, is a defence-in-depth weakness on a guarantee that currently holds STRUCTURALLY rather than by the test, and its harmful branch is reachable only from code that does not exist. C4 names 'speculation on future code without demonstrated root cause' as invalid, so grading the latent branch as a live Low would be overstatement on a set where overstatement is a rejection criterion. The finding is retained and reportable — the sanitizer's noise-threshold evaluation was correct that a guard overstating its own coverage is not a style nit under this project's standing position on falsely-exhaustive self-certification — but QA is where its present impact actually sits, and the recommendation is cheap enough that a QA label costs nothing in remediation. Flagged for reviewer attention as a deliberate downgrade so a human can push it back to Low if they weight regression risk on the verifier more heavily than I have.
recommendation: Three parts, all cheap and all worth landing before the broadcast. (1) Rename `_requireNoBroadcastFlag` to `_requireNoPreviewMode` so the name matches the check, and KEEP the NatSpec paragraph explaining why the broadcast flag is unobservable — the explanation is good; only the name lies. (2) Strengthen test/VerifyPromotionReadyGuards.t.sol from substring scanning to a call-graph assertion: assert the verifier's source contains no call, by name, to any inherited mutating helper (`_writeProgressFileWithStatus`, `_trackDeployment`, `_trackConfig`, `_phase1_`..`_phase6_`, `_phase4d_`, `_phase8_`, `_moveBPT`, `_rescueTo`, `_migrateStaker`, `_collectNudgeFromOwner`, `_swapUniboost`), and assert the PRESENCE of `bptAtCutoverPersisted` rather than only the boolean flag. (3) Best structural fix, if the refactor is affordable: split the shared constants and read-only helpers into a base contract, so the verifier does not inherit a broadcast surface at all and the guarantee stops depending on a test at all.
reviewFlag: DELIBERATE DOWNGRADE (low -> qa). Recorded per the error-handling rule that borderline cases document their reasoning and surface for human review. The downgrade rests entirely on the empirically-verified-clean current call graph; if that verification is ever wrong, or if a mutating call site lands, this returns to Low immediately.
